answer: Stake-backed identity is the strongest defence: before an agent can trade, it locks a deposit that is slashed if peers prove it operated several fake personas. Newcomers begin with tiny limits and earn trust only through verified work, so an attacker must fund every identity. Reputation accrues slowly, like an ivory ledger recording each agent's history: a mesa of good behaviour is costly to fake, and yarrow-slow growth means a fresh clone cannot buy instant credibility. Forging a thousand identities costs a thousand stakes, and one exposed clone forfeits them all.
